> WorkPulse has three kinds of users. Administrators and managers use this web app to organize people and projects, approve time, and handle billing and payroll. Workers, the people whose time is tracked, use the WorkPulse desktop app on Windows, macOS or Linux. It tracks their time and shows them their own timesheet, time off and pay stubs. And your clients can get a read-only client portal that shows the work done for them, without any money. What each person sees depends on their role, so two people can see different menus. That is normal, and we will come back to it later.

*After this chapter, viewers can:* Create an organization, sign in, recover a password, join from an invitation and turn on two-factor sign-in.

**Voiceover**

> To start using WorkPulse, create your organization. Enter your name, the name of your company, your work email and a password of at least ten characters. Then click Create organization. You are the owner of this new organization, and WorkPulse takes you straight to the Overview. For a new organization, the Overview shows a Getting started checklist with five steps: invite your team, create a project, set pay and bill rates, connect the desktop app, and review what is tracked. Each step links to the right page, and it ticks itself off as you go. You can hide the checklist at any time.

### Scene 02.4 — Turn on two-factor sign-in

| | |
|---|---|
| **Duration** | 47 s (narration 45 s) · starts at 3:36 |
| **Recorded as** | Signed out · web app |
| **Clip** | `02.4-turn-on-two-factor-sign-in.webm` |
| **On screen** | Profile › Two-factor authentication: password check, QR code, the 6-digit code, then the recovery codes. |

**Presenter actions (clicks, typing, navigation)**

1. Open the account menu, then Profile & devices, and scroll to Two-factor authentication.
2. Click "Set up", enter the password and click "Continue".
3. Point at the QR code (scan it with an authenticator app).
4. Type the 6-digit code from the app in "Code" and click "Turn on".
5. Point at the recovery codes and the "Download" button.
6. Tick "I have saved these codes somewhere safe" and click "Done".

**Voiceover**

> Protect your account with two-factor sign-in. Open the account menu, choose Profile and devices, and find Two-factor authentication. Click Set up and confirm your password. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app on your phone, such as Google Authenticator or Microsoft Authenticator, then type the six-digit code it shows and click Turn on. WorkPulse now gives you ten recovery codes. Each one works once, if you ever lose your phone. Download them and keep them somewhere safe, tick the box and click Done. From now on, signing in asks for a code from your phone. Administrators can also require two-factor for everyone, which we will see in the security chapter.

**Text overlays:** Callout on the QR code: "Scan with your authenticator app" · Callout on the codes: "Each recovery code works once"

**Zoom and highlight:** Zoom to the QR code. · Zoom to the recovery codes, then to the "Done" button.

**Transition:** Wipe to a chapter card: "Chapter 3 — Finding your way".

| **On screen** | Overview for Avery Admin: This month, Worked today, Waiting for approval, Project budgets and the other cards. |

**Presenter actions (clicks, typing, navigation)**

1. Open the Overview.
2. Point at "This month": Time logged, Est. pay, Billable time, Est. billable.
3. Point at "Worked today".
4. Point at "Waiting for approval".
5. Scroll down through Project budgets and the other cards.
6. Click "Me" in the scope switch, then "All" again.

**Voiceover**

> The Overview is your home page. It updates live, so you always see the current picture. At the top, This month shows the time logged, the estimated pay, the billable time and the estimated amount to bill. Estimates come from your rates and become final once the time is approved. Worked today shows how much your team has tracked so far today. Waiting for approval counts the timesheets and manual time requests that need your decision, and Project budgets warns you before a project runs over. The switch at the top right changes whose numbers you see: everyone, only yourself, or one member.

**Text overlays:** Callout: "Estimates become final after approval" · Callout on the scope switch: "All · Me · Member"

### Scene 04.2 — Time & pay: periods, rules, overtime and break types

| | |
|---|---|
| **Duration** | 48 s (narration 46 s) · starts at 7:50 |
| **Recorded as** | Avery Admin (system admin) · web app |

| **On screen** | Settings › Time & pay: Timesheet period, Timesheet rules, Overtime, Time types and Break types; the "New break type" dialog. |

**Presenter actions (clicks, typing, navigation)**

1. Click the "Time & pay" tab.
2. Point at "Timesheet period" and "Timesheet rules".
3. Scroll to "Overtime" and "Time types".
4. Scroll to "Break types" and click "Add break type".
5. Type "Coffee", switch on "Paid break", type 15 in "Maximum length (minutes)", click "Add break type".
6. Click "Add break type" again: "Lunch", unpaid, 60 minutes.

**Voiceover**

> The Time and pay tab controls how time becomes pay. The timesheet period sets how often members submit their time, for example every week. Timesheet rules can lock old time so it cannot be changed, set minimum hours, and remind people about missing time. Below are the overtime rules and your time types, such as regular or overtime, each with its own pay and bill multiplier. Break types define the breaks your people can take. Let us add a coffee break: name it Coffee, make it a paid break, with a maximum of fifteen minutes. And a lunch break: unpaid, up to sixty minutes. We will plan these breaks on a project in a moment.

**Text overlays:** Callout: "Paid breaks count as paid, non-billable time"

### Scene 04.3 — Choose what the desktop app tracks

| | |
|---|---|
| **Duration** | 46 s (narration 44 s) · starts at 8:38 |
| **Recorded as** | Avery Admin (system admin) · web app |
| **Clip** | `04.3-choose-what-the-desktop-app-tracks.webm` |
| **On screen** | Settings › Tracking policies: the organization default with sections for Tracking, Activity, Idle, Screenshots, Apps and URLs; then the Team scope for one team. |

**Presenter actions (clicks, typing, navigation)**

1. Click the "Tracking policies" tab.
2. Scroll through the Activity, Idle, Screenshots, Apps and URLs sections.
3. Click "Team" in "Policy scope" and choose "Client Success".
4. Point at the screenshot blur setting that this team overrides, and at "Reset to inherited".

**Voiceover**

> Tracking policies decide what the desktop app records. The organization default applies to everyone. Activity counts keyboard and mouse use, never the keys themselves. Idle detection asks people what to do with time when they step away. Screenshots can be switched on, taken a set number of times every ten minutes, and blurred. Apps and URLs record which applications and websites are used. You can override any setting for a team or for one member. Here, the Client Success team has its screenshots blurred. An overridden setting shows Reset to inherited. When you save, the affected members are notified, and each member can always see what is monitored.

**Text overlays:** Callout: "Keystrokes are counted, never recorded" · Callout: "Members are notified of changes"

**Zoom and highlight:** Highlight the "Screenshots" section. · Zoom to the "Policy scope" switch.

**Transition:** Cut to the Roles & permissions tab.

**Voiceover**

> Roles control who can see and do what. The matrix shows every permission for every role. If you need something in between, create a custom role. Give it a name, start from an existing role, and then adjust its permissions. Each permission can apply to the person themselves, their assigned projects, their team, or the whole organization.

## Chapter 6 — Clients, projects and tasks

*After this chapter, viewers can:* Add clients, delete or archive them, share a client portal, create projects with planned breaks, and add tasks.

### Scene 06.1 — Add a client

| | |
|---|---|
| **Duration** | 32 s (narration 30 s) · starts at 11:46 |
| **Recorded as** | Avery Admin (system admin) · web app |
| **Clip** | `06.1-add-a-client.webm` |
| **On screen** | Project Management › Clients and the "New client" dialog. |

**Presenter actions (clicks, typing, navigation)**

1. Open Project Management › Clients and click "New client".
2. Type "Lumen Outdoor Co." in "Company / client name".
3. Type "Rosa Diaz" in "Contact person" and "billing@lumen.example" in "Contact email".
4. Point at Currency, then type 120 in "Bill rate per hour".
5. Click "Create client".

**Voiceover**

> Let us finish with the questions people ask most, all answered in the Help Center. Why are members sent to a download page? Because workers use the desktop app, not the website. Can approved time still be changed? Yes: reopen the timesheet, correct it and approve it again. Once its time is on an invoice, void the invoice first; once it has been paid, correct it with a bonus or deduction on the next payroll. What happens when a computer is offline? The app keeps tracking and sends everything when it is back online. And are keystrokes recorded? No. WorkPulse only counts keyboard and mouse activity. It never records what you type.

4. Open "The Approve button is greyed out".
5. Open "A member doesn’t have the latest desktop app".

**Voiceover**

> Troubleshooting covers the usual problems. A member forgot to stop their timer: force stop it from Live, then edit or split the entry in Time entries. A member's time is missing: check that their app is online, since offline time arrives when they reconnect, and that their computer is approved under Devices. For time they really did not track, add manual time. The Approve button is greyed out: time was added after the timesheet was submitted, so click Request changes and approve it once they resubmit. And if a member does not have the latest desktop app: updates download in the background and install when the member quits the app from its icon in the system tray. Each guide links straight to the page that fixes it.
